title: Danish Magnates
capsule: In the 1333-1352 window this entity denotes the Danish-held Duchy of Estonia (Harrien and Wierland in the north, around Reval/Tallinn), governed in practice by its corporation of vassal magnates after the death of King Christopher II in 1332 left Denmark in a kingless interregnum and absentee rule over its Baltic province. The Estonian nobility was overwhelmingly German-Westphalian in origin, and tensions on the estates helped trigger the St. George's Night Uprising of 1343-1345, in which indigenous Estonians burned manors and besieged Reval before the Teutonic Order crushed the revolt. So weakened, Denmark sold the duchy to the Teutonic Order on 1 November 1346, after which the Danish magnate regime in Estonia gave way to Ordensstaat administration.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Post-1920 boundaries are based on treaty, plebiscite, and formal cartographic records and are well-attested; the 1945 start in this dataset represents the re-emergence of the unoccupied state's full sovereignty and is unambiguous.
